126924.impact: Node capacity metrics are now accurate, preventing pods from being rejected or mis-scheduled due to false capacity exhaustion for the affected volume types. Users of the listed CSI drivers see correct scheduling behavior.

126981.problem: SizeMemoryBackedVolumes was only available as a beta feature behind a feature gate, requiring users to enable the gate to specify sizes for memory‑backed volumes.
126981.affected: Any workloads that define a size for memory‑backed volumes (e.g., EmptyDir, CSI memory volumes) now have the feature enabled by default.
126981.fix: Promoted SizeMemoryBackedVolumes to GA (stable), removing the need for a feature gate and making the API stable for all clusters.
126981.impact: Clusters can now use SizeMemoryBackedVolumes out‑of‑the‑box with guaranteed stability and future compatibility, simplifying storage configuration for memory‑backed volumes such as EmptyDir and CSI memory drivers.

126999.problem: client-go REST calls did not provide contextual logging, so request/response details and the source code location of the caller were missing, making debugging difficult.
126999.affected: Any component or controller that uses the client-go library for Kubernetes API communication.
126999.fix: Added contextual logging to client-go/rest that records request and response information along with the accurate source code location of the caller, improving log granularity.
126999.impact: Developers and operators using client-go (e.g., controllers, operators) can now quickly identify which code path generated a request, easing troubleshooting and enhancing observability of API interactions.

127009.problem: Anonymous authentication endpoints were fixed and could not be customized, limiting administrators from controlling which API paths accept anonymous requests.
127009.affected: Kubernetes clusters using the API server with anonymous authentication; administrators who need to restrict or customize anonymous access.
127009.fix: Graduated the AnonymousAuthConfigurableEndpoints feature gate to beta and enabled it by default, adding configuration options to specify the endpoints that allow anonymous authentication.
127009.impact: Cluster operators can now configure anonymous auth endpoints, improving security flexibility and removing the need to manually enable a beta feature.

127010.problem: The JWT authenticator did not include the JWT's `jti` claim as the `authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id` in the extra fields, so audit logs could not associate requests with a specific JWT credential.
127010.affected: Clusters using JWT token authentication and audit logging; security teams that rely on audit logs to trace token usage.
127010.fix: JWT authenticators now check for a `jti` claim that is a string and, when present, set it as the credential ID (`authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id`). This value is then recorded in audit logs.
127010.impact: Improves traceability and security monitoring by allowing admins to see which specific JWT token was used for a request in audit records, aiding investigations and compliance.

127052.problem: The scheduler did not expose an inflight_events metric for the QueueingHint alpha feature, limiting visibility into how many scheduling events were in flight and making it difficult to observe queueing behavior.
127052.affected: Clusters using the kube-scheduler, especially those that enable the QueueingHint alpha feature and need metrics for monitoring.
127052.fix: The scheduler now emits the inflight_events metric for the QueueingHint feature, providing real‑time counts of in‑flight scheduling events when the feature is enabled.
127052.impact: Operators and developers can monitor and troubleshoot scheduling queueing latency, improve observability of the scheduler, and better tune the QueueingHint feature.

127076.problem: Kubernetes previously built with an older Go version; upgrade required to stay current and benefit from language improvements and security fixes.
127076.affected: All Kubernetes components and any environments that compile Kubernetes from source are affected by the Go version upgrade.
127076.fix: The build system has been updated to compile all Kubernetes binaries with Go 1.23.0.
127076.impact: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are now built with the newer Go toolchain, enabling future improvements and ensuring compatibility with upcoming Go releases. No functional changes for end‑users, but the upgrade may affect developers building from source or custom binaries.

127083.problem: Scheduler plugins had no way to be notified when a pod's scheduling gates were removed or its tolerations changed, limiting their ability to react to these important scheduling-related updates.
127083.affected: Scheduler plugins that need to track pod scheduling‑gate removal or toleration changes; pods whose scheduling gates or tolerations are updated.
127083.fix: Introduced two new cluster events—UpdatePodSchedulingGatesEliminated and UpdatePodTolerations—emitted by the scheduler. Plugins can now watch these events to handle pod scheduling-gate removal and toleration updates.
127083.impact: Plugins can now respond dynamically to changes in pod scheduling constraints, improving custom scheduling logic, observability, and correctness of workloads that depend on these pod attributes.

127093.problem: The RetryGenerateName feature was in beta and required clusters to enable it via the --feature-gates flag on the kube-apiserver. This added configuration overhead and could cause inconsistencies if the flag was omitted.
127093.affected: Any Kubernetes cluster that runs a kube-apiserver, especially those that previously relied on the RetryGenerateName feature gate for name generation of resources like Pods, Deployments, Services, etc.
127093.fix: Promoted RetryGenerateName to GA and enabled it by default in the kube-apiserver. The feature gate flag is no longer needed and will be removed in a future release.
127093.impact: Clusters no longer need to configure the RetryGenerateName feature gate. All API server instances will automatically use the improved name generation logic, simplifying cluster setup and ensuring consistent behavior.

127094.problem: The PreStop lifecycle handler's sleep action could not be set to 0 seconds, causing pods to always wait at least one second or produce an error when a zero duration was specified.
127094.affected: Pods that use a PreStop lifecycle hook with a sleep action, especially when a zero-second delay is desired.
127094.fix: The kubelet now accepts a zero value for the sleep duration in a PreStop handler, allowing immediate continuation without an artificial delay.
127094.impact: Users can define instant termination behavior for containers using PreStop hooks, eliminating unintended pause times and simplifying pod shutdown logic.

127096.problem: When an unknown subcommand name is passed to a parent kubeadm command (e.g., 'kubeadm init phase') or when a parent command that expects subcommands is invoked without specifying one, kubeadm did not return a clear error or list the valid subcommands, leading to confusing behavior for users and scripts.
127096.affected: Anyone using the kubeadm CLI, especially scripts or operators that call commands like 'kubeadm init phase' with incorrect or missing subcommand arguments.
127096.fix: kubeadm now validates subcommand names for all parent commands. If an unknown subcommand is supplied, it returns an explicit error. If a parent command is called without any subcommand, it prints the list of available subcommands and also returns an error.
127096.impact: Users and automation that invoke kubeadm get immediate, actionable feedback for incorrect usage, preventing silent failures and making troubleshooting easier.

127146.problem: There were no built‑in metrics to observe how long Device Resource Allocation (DRA) node operations and the underlying gRPC calls took, making it hard for users to monitor latency or diagnose performance issues.
127146.affected: Clusters using the DRA feature (node‑level device allocation) and any tooling that monitors kubelet metrics.
127146.fix: Adds new Prometheus metrics that record the latency of DRA node‑side operations and the latency of DRA gRPC RPCs, exposing them via the standard metrics endpoint.
127146.impact: Operators can now track DRA performance, set alerts on high latency, and troubleshoot slow device allocation, improving cluster observability and reliability for workloads that rely on DRA.

127155.problem: There was no built‑in metric to show how many containers had their compute resources (e.g., CPUs) aligned by the kubelet, making it difficult for operators to observe and debug CPU manager alignment behavior.
127155.affected: Cluster administrators and developers who rely on kubelet metrics to monitor node resource alignment and CPU manager behavior.
127155.fix: Introduces a new kubelet metric `container_aligned_compute_resources_count` that reports the count of containers whose compute resources are aligned.
127155.impact: Provides operators with direct observability into resource alignment, enabling better troubleshooting, capacity planning, and validation of CPU manager settings on nodes.

127187.problem: The custom profiling feature in `kubectl debug` could be toggled off, leading to inconsistent debugging experiences and potential confusion for users expecting profiling capabilities.
127187.affected: Anyone using `kubectl debug` for pod debugging, especially those who rely on custom profiling for performance analysis.
127187.fix: The feature gate for custom profiling is now locked to `true`, making the feature permanently enabled and immutable in `kubectl debug`.
127187.impact: Users of `kubectl debug` will always have custom profiling available, eliminating the need to manage the feature gate and ensuring reliable, consistent profiling during debugging sessions.

127220.problem: When SchedulerQueueingHint was disabled, in‑tree scheduler plugins subscribed to all node update events, even those unrelated to scheduling (e.g., status changes). This caused unnecessary processing, higher memory usage, and slower reaction to relevant cluster events.
127220.affected: All clusters that run the default in‑tree scheduler plugins and enable SchedulerQueueingHint. Workloads that depend on taints, tolerations, or node resource changes benefit from quicker scheduling decisions.
127220.fix: With SchedulerQueueingHint enabled, the in‑tree plugins now subscribe only to node updates that affect scheduling decisions—taint changes, toleration updates, and allocatable resource changes. Updates that do not modify these fields are ignored, allowing the scheduler to requeue pods only when needed.
127220.impact: The scheduler reacts to relevant node changes faster and with lower memory overhead, improving overall cluster performance and scalability, especially in clusters with frequent node status churn.

127228.problem: The job controller's event handlers, especially the update handler, were significantly slower than other controllers (≈3 ms per event). This caused the internal work queue's ring buffer to grow unbounded under high job churn, leading to increased CPU usage and potential controller lag.
127228.affected: Clusters that run many Job objects or experience rapid job creation/deletion (e.g., CI pipelines, batch processing systems). The slowdown primarily affected the controller-manager's job controller.
127228.fix: Optimized the job controller's handling of job update events, moving heavy logic out of the event handler and streamlining the processing path, resulting in faster event handling.
127228.impact: Reduces CPU pressure and prevents work‑queue buildup in clusters with many rapidly changing Job objects, improving stability and scalability for batch workloads.

127242.problem: kubeadm upgrade node did not expose separate phases for handling addon upgrades or post-upgrade tasks, so users could not explicitly run or skip the addon upgrade step during node upgrades.
127242.affected: Administrators using kubeadm to upgrade worker nodes; any clusters upgraded with kubeadm where addon upgrades are required.
127242.fix: Added support for new `addon` and `post-upgrade` phases in `kubeadm upgrade node`. Users can now run `kubeadm upgrade node phase addon` to perform addon upgrades or use `--skip-phases addon` to skip them. The `post-upgrade` phase is currently a no‑op placeholder for future release‑specific actions.
127242.impact: Cluster administrators gain fine‑grained control over node upgrade workflows, enabling them to manage addon upgrades independently or defer them when needed, and provides a hook for future post‑upgrade tasks.

127302.problem: The StrictCostEnforcementForVAP and StrictCostEnforcementForWebhooks feature gates were in beta/alpha and not enabled by default, limiting users from having consistent, strict cost enforcement for ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and admission webhooks.
127302.affected: All clusters that run the API server, especially those that use ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or admission webhooks, will see the new strict cost enforcement behavior.
127302.fix: Promote both feature gates to GA, making strict cost enforcement enabled by default and stable across releases.
127302.impact: Clusters will now have consistent, enforced cost checks for VAP and webhook admission paths, improving reliability and predictability of admission decisions without requiring manual feature‑gate enablement.

127326.problem: External components had no built‑in way to obtain the CA bundle that signs kube‑apiserver serving certificates, making verification of the API server’s TLS certs cumbersome and error‑prone.
127326.affected: Any workload or external client that needs to validate the kube‑apiserver's serving certificate – e.g., ingress controllers, service meshes, custom users of the API, and automated tooling.
127326.fix: The control‑plane trust‑anchor publisher now creates and manages a dedicated ClusterTrustBundle object linked to the `kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-serving` X.509 signer. The Bundle’s payload holds the PEM‑encoded CA bundle that can be used to verify kube‑apiserver serving certificates.
127326.impact: Clients, proxies, and tooling can programmatically retrieve the trusted CA bundle from the ClusterTrustBundle, simplifying TLS verification, improving security posture, and supporting automated trust distribution across clusters.

127348.problem: The LoadBalancerIPMode feature was only available in beta/alpha, so clusters could not rely on it for production workloads and had to enable a feature gate.
127348.affected: Clusters that create Services of type LoadBalancer and want to control IP mode (shared vs per‑service) could not use the feature in production until it was GA.
127348.fix: Promoted LoadBalancerIPMode to GA, removing the feature gate and stabilizing the API, making the feature generally available for production use.
127348.impact: Users can now use the LoadBalancerIPMode option on Services without any feature‑gate toggles, benefiting from a stable, supported implementation suitable for production environments.

127378.problem: The job controller in kube-controller-manager processed job delete events inefficiently, leading to increased latency and high CPU usage when many Jobs were deleted.
127378.affected: Clusters that run a large number of Job resources, especially those that frequently create and delete Jobs (e.g., batch processing pipelines).
127378.fix: Optimized the job controller's event handling path for job deletions, reducing the amount of work performed per delete event and lowering overall processing overhead.
127378.impact: Job deletions complete faster and the controller manager consumes less CPU, improving cluster responsiveness for workloads that create and delete many Jobs.

127388.problem: The metadata client List() in client-go could not use API streaming, causing slower performance when fetching large collections of objects.
127388.affected: Applications using the client-go metadata client to list large numbers of objects; they must enable the WatchListClient feature gate and run against a server that supports streaming.
127388.fix: Added a new WatchListClient feature gate that enables API streaming for List() calls. When the feature is enabled and the API server supports streaming, the client streams results; otherwise it falls back to the traditional list verb.
127388.impact: Clients that list many resources can retrieve data faster and with reduced API server load, improving scalability for tools that rely on bulk metadata retrieval.

127404.problem: Windows nodes did not support graceful shutdown, so when a Windows node was stopped or rebooted pods were terminated abruptly without a termination period, leading to potential data loss or incomplete cleanup.
127404.affected: Users running Windows workloads on Kubernetes clusters. Specifically, any pod scheduled on a Windows node that may be affected by node power‑off or reboot events.
127404.fix: Implemented and enabled the graceful shutdown feature for Windows nodes, allowing the kubelet to send termination signals to pods and respect their terminationGracePeriodSeconds during node shutdown.
127404.impact: Pods on Windows nodes now have a chance to shut down cleanly, run pre‑stop hooks, and persist state, improving reliability and reducing risk of data loss during node shutdown or reboot.

127444.problem: The NodeAffinity scheduler plugin's QueueingHint considered unrelated node changes, causing pods with node affinity to remain unschedulable longer than necessary.
127444.affected: Pods with node affinity rules, and any workloads that rely on node selection, could experience delayed scheduling when unrelated node changes occurred.
127444.fix: The QueueHint logic was updated to ignore node changes that do not affect the pod's affinity constraints, allowing the scheduler to re-evaluate pods only when relevant node state changes occur.
127444.impact: Pods that use node affinity are scheduled more quickly, reducing scheduling latency and improving overall cluster throughput, especially in clusters with frequent unrelated node updates.

127473.problem: The NodeResourceFit scheduling plugin’s QueueHint logic considered node changes that were unrelated to a pending pod, causing the pod to remain unschedulable longer than necessary.
127473.affected: Any workload with pods that rely on the NodeResourceFit plugin for placement, especially clusters with frequent node‑resource updates.
127473.fix: The plugin now ignores node changes that do not affect the pod’s resource fit when updating QueueHint, allowing the scheduler to re‑evaluate the pod promptly.
127473.impact: Pods that were previously stuck in an unschedulable state due to irrelevant node updates are now scheduled faster, improving overall scheduling efficiency and reducing wait times for workloads.

127483.problem: Node administrators could not guarantee that CPUs listed in `reservedSystemCPUs` would be used exclusively by system daemons and interrupt handling; the static CPU manager could still assign those cores to pod workloads, leading to potential performance interference.
127483.affected: Node operators and workload owners who need guaranteed isolation of system‑reserved CPUs, especially on performance‑critical or real‑time workloads.
127483.fix: Introduced the `strict-cpu-reservation` flag for the static CPU manager policy. When enabled, any CPU core listed in `reservedSystemCPUs` is locked for system daemons and interrupt processing only and cannot be allocated to pods.
127483.impact: Provides deterministic CPU isolation for system services, improving real‑time and latency‑sensitive workloads on NUMA‑aware nodes. Users can now enforce strict separation without custom patches or external tooling.

127489.problem: Pods could not set the per‑pod sysctls net.ipv4.tcp_rmem and net.ipv4.tcp_wmem because these sysctls were not on the safe‑sysctl list, even though kernels ≥4.15 made them namespaced and thus configurable per pod.
127489.affected: Pods running on nodes with Linux kernel ≥4.15 that need custom TCP buffer settings, especially high‑connection workloads like databases.
127489.fix: Add net.ipv4.tcp_rmem and net.ipv4.tcp_wmem to the default safe‑sysctl list for clusters running kernel 4.15 or newer. The sysctls are now allowed by default and are permitted in the baseline and restricted Pod Security Admission policies starting with v1.32.
127489.impact: Applications that need to tune TCP buffer sizes (e.g., Cassandra, high‑throughput services) can now configure these settings per pod without modifying kubelet arguments or node‑wide sysctl values, improving performance and simplifying deployment.

127506.problem: There was no built‑in metric to expose the state of CPU pools managed by the CPU manager when the static policy is enabled, making it hard for operators to monitor and troubleshoot CPU allocation.
127506.affected: Cluster administrators, monitoring systems, and any workloads using the static CPU manager policy that need visibility into CPU pool allocation.
127506.fix: Introduced a new kubelet metric that reports information about the static CPU manager pools, providing visibility into how CPUs are assigned to pods.
127506.impact: Operators can now monitor CPU pool usage via Prometheus or other metric collectors, set alerts, and better understand resource fragmentation, improving reliability and capacity planning for workloads relying on the static CPU manager policy.

127524.problem: Consumers of the discovery client lacked a convenient way to list API groups, requiring manual parsing of discovery data.
127524.affected: Any component or custom controller that uses client-go discovery to enumerate API groups.
127524.fix: Added a GroupLister interface to the discovery GroupManager, providing a dedicated method to retrieve the list of API groups.
127524.impact: Simplifies and standardizes group discovery for controllers, operators, and other clients, reducing boilerplate and potential parsing errors.

127566.problem: When the kubelet becomes unresponsive, there was no lightweight, automatic way for systemd to detect and restart it, leading to hung nodes that required manual intervention or external health‑check scripts.
127566.affected: Clusters running the kubelet as a systemd service on Linux nodes. A hung kubelet would previously require manual or script‑based recovery.
127566.fix: Implemented integration of the systemd watchdog API into the kubelet. The kubelet now periodically updates the watchdog timer using the same checks performed by the /healthz endpoint, allowing systemd to automatically restart a hung kubelet.
127566.impact: Nodes managed by systemd can now self‑heal from kubelet hangs without external health‑check wrappers, improving cluster stability, reducing downtime, and lowering operational overhead for operators.

127574.problem: When running e2e-node tests with the remote option, the tests always use the default network. In environments where that network is saturated or unavailable, the tests cannot be executed.
127574.affected: Users of the e2e-node test framework who run tests with the remote option and need a non‑default network.
127574.fix: Added a new flag/parameter that allows callers to specify a custom network (or subnet) to be used for remote e2e-node test runs.
127574.impact: Test runners can now choose an appropriate network, avoiding conflicts and improving test reliability in diverse cluster environments.

127611.problem: Kubernetes builds previously used an older Go version, which could cause build failures, miss out on language improvements, and lack recent security fixes.
127611.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source, including CI systems and developers; no runtime impact on clusters.
127611.fix: The build process has been updated to compile Kubernetes with Go 1.23.1.
127611.impact: Developers and CI pipelines can now build Kubernetes with the latest Go tooling, gaining security patches, performance improvements, and better support for newer platforms.

127661.problem: There were no built‑in metrics exposing how many ResourceClaims exist in a cluster or how many are currently allocated, making it hard for operators to observe DRA usage and set alerts.
127661.affected: Clusters that use Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) and create ResourceClaims, as well as administrators who need visibility into claim usage.
127661.fix: The resource claim controller now publishes Prometheus‑compatible metrics for the total number of ResourceClaims and for the subset that are allocated.
127661.impact: Operators can monitor DRA resource consumption, detect allocation issues early, and create alerts or dashboards, improving cluster observability and capacity planning.

127786.problem: local-up-cluster.sh did not provide a way to enable leader election for control plane components, making it impossible to test leader election behavior in a local cluster setup.
127786.affected: Users who run local-up-cluster.sh (e.g., developers, CI jobs) who need to test leader election and high‑availability behavior of control‑plane components.
127786.fix: Added a LEADER_ELECT command‑line flag to local-up-cluster.sh that enables leader election for the control‑plane components when the script is run.
127786.impact: Developers and CI pipelines can now simulate production‑like leader election scenarios on a local cluster, improving testing of failover and HA behavior without needing a full multi‑node environment.

127861.problem: A newer Go version used in the build caused compatibility or build issues, leading to an undesirable change in the Kubernetes binaries.
127861.affected: Developers and CI systems that build Kubernetes; downstream distributors and users of the released binaries.
127861.fix: Reverted the Go compiler version back to Go 1.23.0 for building all Kubernetes components.
127861.impact: Restores reliable builds and ensures that released binaries are compatible with existing toolchains and CI pipelines, preventing potential build failures or subtle runtime bugs introduced by the newer Go version.

128029.problem: Sidecar containers were assigned an OOM score adjustment higher than regular containers in the same pod due to incorrect calculation, causing them to be killed first during memory pressure, contrary to documentation and expectations.
128029.affected: Pods that include sidecar containers, especially those using burstable QoS, could lose sidecars before primary containers under memory pressure.
128029.fix: Updated the kubelet's OOM score adjustment logic so sidecar containers receive an oom_score_adj that is equal to or lower than that of regular containers in the pod, aligning OOM killing order with intended behavior.
128029.impact: Ensures sidecar processes (e.g., logging, monitoring, proxy agents) remain alive longer during memory pressure, improving pod reliability and matching documented OOM eviction semantics for burstable QoS pods.

128031.problem: Kubeadm always wrote the CRI socket path as an annotation on the Node object and did not generate a per‑node kubelet instance configuration, making it impossible to customize the containerRuntimeEndpoint for each node (e.g., when using a node‑local CRI socket).
128031.affected: Clusters that enable the `NodeLocalCRISocket` feature gate, particularly during kubeadm init/join. Users who need per‑node CRI socket customization are directly impacted.
128031.fix: Introduce the `NodeLocalCRISocket` feature gate. When enabled, kubeadm creates `/var/lib/kubelet/instance-config.yaml` on each node to set the `containerRuntimeEndpoint` in the kubelet config and stops adding the CRI socket annotation to the Node object.
128031.impact: Allows clusters to run a distinct CRI socket per node (common with node‑local container runtimes), simplifying configuration and avoiding stale or duplicated Node annotations. Improves flexibility for custom runtime setups without affecting existing behavior when the feature gate is off.

128046.problem: PodLifecycleSleepAction was only available as a beta feature, so users could not rely on it for production workloads due to potential API changes or missing guarantees.
128046.affected: Any workloads that define a PodLifecycleSleepAction (e.g., pods using a preStop sleep hook) can now rely on the feature in production.
128046.fix: The PodLifecycleSleepAction feature has been graduated to GA, making the API and its behavior stable and fully supported in production clusters.
128046.impact: Clusters can now safely use PodLifecycleSleepAction in pod specifications without fearing future incompatibilities, enabling reliable sleep actions during pod termination.

128053.problem: The WatchList functionality was only available as an alpha feature gate and was not enabled for the controller manager, limiting its reliability and usability for users needing stable watch handling.
128053.affected: Clusters using kube-apiserver and controller-manager that rely on watch semantics; developers building controllers or operators that benefit from the optimized WatchList client.
128053.fix: Graduates the WatchList feature gate to Beta for kube-apiserver and enables the WatchListClient in the kube-controller-manager, making the feature stable and usable by default.
128053.impact: Provides a more stable, performant watch mechanism for API consumers and controllers, reducing watch latency and improving scalability of watch-intensive workloads.

128110.affected: All Kubernetes components compiled from source (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.)
128110.fix: Kubernetes build process updated to compile the codebase with Go 1.23.2 instead of the previous Go version.
128110.impact: All Kubernetes binaries are now built with a newer Go compiler, bringing any upstream compiler improvements, security fixes, and ensuring future compatibility with Go ecosystem updates.

128124.problem: The TopologyManagerPolicyOptions feature was only available behind a feature gate, requiring users to enable the flag to use it.
128124.affected: Users running kubelet on nodes who wanted to use TopologyManagerPolicyOptions but previously had to enable the feature gate.
128124.fix: Promoted the TopologyManagerPolicyOptions feature-flag to GA, removing the need for an explicit feature gate and making the functionality generally available by default.
128124.impact: Clusters can now use TopologyManagerPolicyOptions without extra configuration, providing stable, out‑of‑the‑box support for NUMA‑aware pod placement and resource management.

128168.problem: Node API clients authenticated with kubelet credentials could read any Node or Pod objects. The new AuthorizeNodeWithSelectors behavior now restricts nodes to only their own Node object and Pods scheduled on them, breaking clients that relied on broader read access.
128168.affected: Clients (including custom controllers or monitoring tools) that used kubelet credentials to read other Node or Pod objects, as well as the nodes themselves, are affected by the stricter authorizer rules.
128168.fix: Promoted AuthorizeWithSelectors and AuthorizeNodeWithSelectors to beta. The node authorizer now enforces field and label selector checks, limiting node clients to their own resources. Users must update authentication credentials, adjust client usage, or grant separate read permissions outside the node authorizer.
128168.impact: Improves cluster security by enforcing least‑privilege access for node credentials and prevents nodes from querying unrelated resources. Clusters that used kubelet credentials to inspect other nodes or pods must update their auth setup or permissions.

128169.problem: Service account tokens did not include a unique identifier (jti) or node information, and tokens bound directly to nodes were not validated, limiting auditability, token revocation, and security enforcement.
128169.affected: Any workload or component that uses service account tokens for pod authentication, especially those that bind tokens to specific nodes or need token revocation/auditing.
128169.fix: Promoted three features to GA: ServiceAccountTokenJTI adds a jti claim and exposes it via authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id; ServiceAccountTokenPodNodeInfo adds node name and uid claims to pod-mounted tokens and exposes them via authentication.kubernetes.io/node-name and node-uid; ServiceAccountTokenNodeBindingValidation enforces validation of service account tokens that are bound directly to nodes.
128169.impact: Improves security and observability of service account token usage by enabling token traceability, node-aware authentication decisions, and ensuring node-bound tokens are correctly validated. This benefits clusters that rely on service account authentication for pods, especially in multi‑tenant or high‑security environments.

128186.problem: During upgrades, version skew between kubelet and scheduler could cause in-place pod vertical scaling (resource resize) to be incorrectly processed when the feature gate is disabled, leading to resize attempts that are infeasible or inconsistent state.
128186.affected: Pods that use InPlacePodVerticalScaling (in‑place resource resize) and clusters undergoing upgrades where kubelet and scheduler may run different versions of the feature gate.
128186.fix: Implemented version‑skew handling for the InPlacePodVerticalScaling beta graduation: kubelet now rejects a proposed resize as Infeasible when the feature gate is off, and the scheduler uses the max of ResourcesAllocated and Requests when a PodStatus.Resize field is set, regardless of the feature‑gate state.
128186.impact: Ensures pods are not incorrectly resized during component version mismatches, preventing pod failures or stuck resize operations and making upgrades that involve the feature gate safer and more reliable.

128190.problem: kube-apiserver could only sign service account tokens internally and had no mechanism to fetch public verifying keys from an external signer, limiting flexibility and integration with external key management solutions.
128190.affected: Clusters that require external signing of service account tokens or want to integrate with external key management services. Existing workloads continue to use the internal signer unless the feature gate is enabled.
128190.fix: Introduced the alpha ExternalServiceAccountTokenSigner feature gate and a new --service-account-signing-endpoint flag. When enabled, the apiserver can delegate token signing and key retrieval to an external service via a Unix domain socket (file system or abstract namespace).
128190.impact: Clusters can now offload service account token signing to external systems (e.g., HSMs, external signing services), improving security posture and allowing custom signing workflows. It also enables retrieval of the public key for token verification, facilitating integration with external identity providers.

128287.problem: In the beta release of in-place pod vertical scaling, guaranteed Pods with integer CPU requests could be resized on nodes that have a static CPU & Memory allocation policy, which is unsupported and could lead to undefined behavior.
128287.affected: Clusters using the beta in‑place vertical scaling feature with guaranteed Pods that request whole CPUs on nodes that have a static CPU & Memory policy.
128287.fix: Add a validation that blocks in‑place resize for guaranteed Pods with integer CPU requests when the node is configured with a static CPU & Memory policy. The change is gated by the feature flag `InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs`, which defaults to false and can be enabled for development work.
128287.impact: Prevents users from attempting unsupported in‑place vertical scaling operations, avoiding potential pod failures or node resource mis‑allocation. Developers can still enable the gate to continue work on the feature.

128342.problem: During online expansion of raw block CSI volumes, kubelet invoked the NodeExpandVolume CSI RPC even when the driver indicated NodeExpansionRequired=false in the ControllerExpandVolumeResponse, leading to unnecessary calls and potential expansion failures.
128342.affected: Users running CSI drivers that support raw block volumes with online expansion (e.g., vSphere CSI driver) and any workloads using such PVCs.
128342.fix: The RecoverVolumeExpansionFailure feature gate (now promoted to beta) adds logic to respect the NodeExpansionRequired flag and to recover from volume expansion failures, preventing spurious NodeExpandVolume calls.
128342.impact: Reduces needless CSI traffic and eliminates false expansion errors, making volume expansion more reliable for block‑mode volumes and improving overall storage operation stability.

128387.problem: The pod index labels for StatefulSets (apps.kubernetes.io/pod-index) and for Indexed Jobs (batch.kubernetes.io/job-completion-index) were only beta, so users could not depend on them for stable selectors, scheduling, or monitoring.
128387.affected: Operators and developers using StatefulSets or Indexed Jobs who need pod index information for selectors, scheduling, or monitoring.
128387.fix: Both labels are promoted to stable. The controllers now always add these labels to Pods created by StatefulSets and Indexed Jobs, and the API server treats them as stable fields.
128387.impact: Users can now reliably use these labels in pod selectors, affinity rules, monitoring, and automation without worrying about future incompatibility, improving workload management and observability.

128415.problem: The previous watch cache implementation for LIST verbs used a less efficient data structure, leading to suboptimal performance and scalability for list and watch operations.
128415.affected: Any workload, controller, or tool that performs LIST or WATCH API calls against the kube-apiserver.
128415.fix: Introduced a new watch cache implementation based on a b‑tree data structure. It is enabled by default; users can disable it by turning off the BtreeWatchCache feature gate.
128415.impact: Improves latency, throughput, and memory usage of LIST/WATCH API calls, benefiting controllers, operators, and kubectl users without requiring any changes. An opt‑out path is provided for any regressions.

128444.problem: The DaemonSet controller used a hard‑coded concurrency of only 2 worker threads, which could become a bottleneck in large clusters or when many DaemonSets are present, causing delays in pod creation for critical system DaemonSets.
128444.affected: Clusters with many DaemonSets or large numbers of nodes, especially those relying on system DaemonSets (e.g., CNI plugin installers).
128444.fix: Introduces the `--concurrent-daemonset-syncs` flag to kube‑controller‑manager, allowing operators to set the number of worker threads the DaemonSet controller uses at runtime.
128444.impact: Admins can tune DaemonSet sync parallelism to match cluster size, improving pod scheduling speed, preventing node‑ready delays, and increasing overall cluster scalability and reliability.

128472.problem: SchedulerQueueingHints was only available as an alpha feature that required manually enabling a feature gate, making it harder for users to benefit from the improved scheduling behavior.
128472.affected: Any cluster that uses the scheduler; users who previously had to enable the feature gate manually now get the functionality automatically.
128472.fix: The feature has been graduated to beta and the feature gate is now enabled by default, so the queueing hints logic is active in all clusters without additional configuration.
128472.impact: Clusters automatically get the performance and fairness improvements provided by queueing hints, reducing scheduling latency and improving pod placement decisions without any extra steps from users.

128517.problem: The kubelet memory manager was only available in alpha/beta with feature gates, limiting its use in production clusters and requiring manual enablement.
128517.affected: All Kubernetes clusters that run kubelet and want stable memory management for pods; especially workloads that rely on memory limits and QoS.
128517.fix: Graduated the memory manager to GA: it is now enabled by default, has a stable API, and no longer requires feature‑gate flags, making it production‑ready.
128517.impact: Clusters can reliably use the memory manager to enforce pod memory limits, improve QoS enforcement, and reduce out‑of‑memory incidents without extra configuration.

128533.problem: The previous version of the system-validators library (pre‑v1.9.1) could incorrectly reject or miss certain node‑level configuration issues, leading to validation errors during node startup or when applying node policies.
128533.affected: Kubernetes nodes that run the kubelet and rely on system‑validators for node‑level checks. Clusters using the default node validation flow are impacted.
128533.fix: Updates the vendored system‑validators dependency to v1.9.1, which contains fixes for the validation logic and improves compatibility with current node components.
128533.impact: Nodes can now start and operate with correct validation of system configuration, reducing false‑positive failures and ensuring node health checks work as expected.

128539.problem: Kubernetes API server and storage only supported JSON and protobuf encoding, so users could not use CBOR (Concise Binary Object Representation) for API request/response bodies or for persisting custom resources.
128539.affected: Clusters that need CBOR encoding for API traffic or custom resource storage; client-go applications that want to use CBOR must opt‑in.
128539.fix: Introduced the CBORServingAndStorage feature gate. When enabled, the API server can serve and accept CBOR-encoded payloads and store custom resources in CBOR. Client-go provides corresponding feature gates (ClientsAllowCBOR and ClientsPreferCBOR) so applications can opt‑in to CBOR.
128539.impact: Enables more efficient binary encoding, reducing request/response size and storage footprint for custom resources. Gives users flexibility to choose CBOR where it offers performance or bandwidth benefits.

128556.problem: Kubelet had no metric to track how many pods were rejected during admission, making it difficult to detect regressions or diagnose admission‑related failures.
128556.affected: Kubelet users and cluster operators who rely on metrics to observe pod admission health.
128556.fix: Introduces a new counter metric `kubelet_admission_rejections_total` on the kubelet, incremented for each pod rejected during admission. The metric includes a `reason` label indicating why the pod was rejected.
128556.impact: Operators can now monitor, alert on, and investigate spikes in admission rejections, improving cluster reliability and troubleshooting of pod scheduling issues.

128560.problem: Windows nodes lacked support for the kubelet’s node memory manager, preventing memory allocation enforcement and memory-aware scheduling for Windows workloads.
128560.affected: Clusters with Windows nodes; Windows pods that require memory limits or memory-aware scheduling.
128560.fix: Implemented the node memory manager for Windows, adding the necessary code paths and integration so that Windows nodes can participate in memory management and affinity features.
128560.impact: Windows workloads can now benefit from memory limits, memory-aware pod placement, and overall better resource isolation, bringing Windows node behavior in line with Linux nodes.

128640.problem: Kubelet's periodic node status updates are aligned across nodes, causing all nodes to send status reports at the same interval (default 5 minutes). This creates spikes in API server CPU usage, especially in large clusters with thousands of nodes.
128640.affected: Clusters with many nodes (e.g., thousands) that use the default nodeStatusReportFrequency and experience API server CPU spikes every 5 minutes due to synchronized status updates.
128640.fix: Kubelet now adds a one‑time random delay of up to 50 % of the nodeStatusReportFrequency when it starts. This staggers the first status report, spreading subsequent periodic updates evenly over the reporting window.
128640.impact: API server load becomes smoother, avoiding periodic CPU spikes and improving scalability and stability for large clusters.

128852.problem: No functional issue; this change updates the Go compiler used to build Kubernetes binaries to version 1.23.3.
128852.affected: All Kubernetes components (apiserver, scheduler, controller‑manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube‑proxy, etc.) are rebuilt with the newer Go version.
128852.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.23.3, replacing the previous Go version.
128852.impact: Provides security, performance, and compatibility improvements from the newer Go release and ensures future development can rely on the latest Go toolchain. No runtime behavior change for clusters.

129081.problem: Kubernetes did not propagate the request UID via HTTP headers to downstream components, limiting request tracing and correlation across API server extensions and other services.
129081.affected: Clusters that use aggregated API servers, admission webhooks, or other remote request handlers that need request correlation. The feature is optional and controlled via a feature gate.
129081.fix: Introduced request header UID propagation behind the new alpha feature gate `RemoteRequestHeaderUID`. When the gate is enabled, the apiserver adds the request UID to outgoing HTTP headers, and downstream components can read it.
129081.impact: Enables better observability and debugging of multi‑component request flows, improving auditability and troubleshooting for users that rely on extension API servers or other remote request handling.

125634.problem: Audit logs did not include a stable identifier for X.509 client certificate authentication, making it hard to correlate requests with specific client certificates for security analysis and debugging.
125634.affected: Clusters that use X.509 client certificates for API authentication and rely on audit logs for security or troubleshooting.
125634.fix: The kube-apiserver now derives a credential ID from the certificate's signature and includes this ID in audit log entries for X.509 client certificate authentication.
125634.impact: Administrators can now reliably link audit events to the exact client certificate used, improving security auditing, incident investigation, and compliance reporting.

125982.problem: Kubelet did not provide a way to configure compressible resources (e.g., memory compression) for system-reserved and kube-reserved cgroup slices, limiting fine‑grained resource accounting and over‑commit handling on nodes.
125982.affected: Kubelet on nodes that use system‑reserved or kube‑reserved resource slices; workloads that rely on accurate reserved resource accounting.
125982.fix: Adds a compressible resource setting to the system‑reserved and kube‑reserved slices, allowing administrators to specify compressible resource limits for those reserved resources.
125982.impact: Node administrators can now correctly account for and limit compressible resources in reserved slices, improving node resource management, preventing unexpected resource pressure, and enabling better utilization of memory compression features.

126096.problem: When a single process inside a container was OOM‑killed on nodes using cgroups v2, the kubelet treated it as a container‑wide OOM event and terminated all remaining processes in that container, causing unnecessary loss of work.
126096.affected: Kubernetes nodes that use cgroups v2 (Linux/Windows) and workloads that run multiple processes in a single container.
126096.fix: Introduced the `singleProcessOOMKill` boolean flag in the kubelet configuration. When set to true, the kubelet enables per‑process OOM killing on cgroups v2, so only the offending process is killed while the rest of the container continues to run.
126096.impact: Improves workload reliability for users running containers on cgroups v2 (Linux and Windows) by preventing a single OOM‑killed process from bringing down the entire container, reducing unnecessary restarts and improving resource utilization.

126347.problem: Kubelet's API only exposed a coarse 'nodes/proxy' permission, forcing users to grant broad access to fetch health, pod list, or config, which violated the principle of least privilege and could enable privilege escalation.
126347.affected: Administrators configuring RBAC for node resources; workloads that need health checks, pod listings, or kubelet config access; any cluster that enables the KubeletFineGrainedAuthz feature gate.
126347.fix: Introduced fine‑grained kubelet subresources (nodes/healthz, nodes/pods, nodes/configz) behind the KubeletFineGrainedAuthz feature gate, allowing RBAC policies to grant access to each endpoint individually.
126347.impact: Clusters can now enforce least‑privilege RBAC for kubelet endpoints, reducing attack surface and avoiding unnecessary exec/run/attach permissions while still allowing health checks and pod/config queries.

126977.problem: CRD validation expressions could not reference fields whose names matched CEL reserved keywords, forcing developers to rename fields or use indirect workarounds.
126977.affected: Authors of CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs) and clusters that rely on CRD validation expressions that need to reference fields named with CEL reserved words.
126977.fix: The CEL library integration for CRD validation now allows reserved keywords to be used directly as field names in object validation expressions, supporting the name‑format CEL library syntax.
126977.impact: Makes authoring CRD validation rules simpler and more intuitive, reducing boilerplate and potential errors for developers building custom resources.

127134.problem: Kubernetes lacked a built-in, extensible mutating admission mechanism that could be expressed via CEL, limiting administrators to static or custom webhook solutions for request mutation.
127134.affected: Cluster administrators and developers who need to mutate resources during admission. Works with any workload that passes through the API server admission chain.
127134.fix: Introduces a new v1alpha1 admissionregistration.k8s.io API for MutatingAdmissionPolicy objects. When the MutatingAdmissionPolicy feature gate and runtime-config are enabled, users can define mutating admission policies using CEL expressions, allowing declarative, extensible request mutation without custom webhooks.
127134.impact: Provides a native, declarative way to perform request mutation, reducing operational complexity and improving performance for clusters that need dynamic admission control. Enables easier policy authoring and potential future enhancements to admission control semantics.

127167.problem: Kubernetes API validation rejected pod DNS search domains that were a single dot (".") or contained an underscore ("_") even though these are valid in some DNS configurations, preventing pods from using such search domains.
127167.affected: Any pod that needs a search domain of '.' or that includes '_' in its search domain list. Clusters using custom DNS configurations that rely on these patterns were previously unable to create such pods.
127167.fix: Updated the pod spec validation logic to accept a single dot and underscore characters in DNS search domain entries, aligning the validation with DNS RFCs and real‑world usage.
127167.impact: Pods can now successfully use '.' or '_' in their DNS search domain lists, enabling workloads that rely on these naming patterns (e.g., certain internal DNS setups) to resolve names correctly without workarounds.

127360.problem: The PodLog API only returned combined stdout and stderr streams, so users could not request a specific log stream (stdout or stderr) directly, forcing them to filter logs themselves.
127360.affected: Any client or tool that reads container logs via the `/log` endpoint (e.g., `kubectl logs`, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring agents) can now request a specific stream.
127360.fix: Introduced a new `Stream` field in `PodLogOptions` that lets clients specify which stream to retrieve (stdout or stderr). The API now accepts this field, with the caveat that using `Stream` together with `TailLines` is not supported.
127360.impact: Enables more precise log retrieval, simplifying debugging and log processing for tools and users that need only one stream. Improves observability workflows while noting a limitation with TailLines.

127511.problem: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) API version was promoted to v1beta1 and set as the storage version, making the new version unreadable by older clusters. While upgrades are safe, downgrading from 1.32 to 1.31 with any DRA objects (ResourceClaims, ResourceClaimTemplates, DeviceClasses, ResourceSlices) is not supported.
127511.affected: Clusters that have created DRA objects (ResourceClaims, ResourceClaimTemplates, DeviceClasses, ResourceSlices) and any workloads relying on those resources. Downgrade operations from 1.32 to 1.31 are affected.
127511.fix: The change introduces the v1beta1 API as the storage version for DRA, enabling beta‑grade features. No action is required for upgrades; users must avoid downgrades that contain DRA resources or delete those resources before downgrading.
127511.impact: Clusters using DRA resources must not downgrade across the 1.32 boundary, preventing potential loss of DRA objects and ensuring API compatibility. Upgrade paths remain seamless, but downgrade plans need to account for DRA objects.

127513.problem: When a resource stored in etcd is corrupted (e.g., decryption failure or decoding error), the API server cannot read it and normal DELETE requests fail, leaving the object stuck in the cluster.
127513.affected: Clusters that contain resources that cannot be read from storage (e.g., due to encryption or decoding errors). Administrators attempting to delete such resources are affected.
127513.fix: Introduce a gated feature (AllowUnsafeMalformedObjectDeletion) and a new DELETE option `ignoreStoreReadErrorWithClusterBreakingPotential`. When enabled, the API server will perform an unsafe delete that bypasses finalizers and precondition checks, allowing the corrupt object to be removed. The LIST response’s Status.details now includes identifiers for corrupt objects.
127513.impact: Cluster administrators can recover from stuck corrupt resources without needing to manually tamper with etcd, reducing downtime. The operation is optional and risky, so it is disabled by default and clearly labeled as potentially cluster‑breaking.

127581.problem: There was no HTTP endpoint to retrieve the command‑line flags with which kube‑apiserver was started, making it hard for operators and tools to discover the server’s configuration at runtime.
127581.affected: Kubernetes administrators and any tooling that needs to inspect the apiserver’s runtime flags.
127581.fix: Introduces a new `/flagz` endpoint on the kube‑apiserver that returns the current flag values in a human‑readable format.
127581.impact: Operators can now easily view and verify the apiserver’s flag configuration via the API, improving debugging, observability, and automation tooling without needing access to the process command line.

127587.problem: Watch clients that rely on synthetic Bookmark events did not receive any information about the initial events list format, making it difficult for them to correctly initialize state when starting a watch.
127587.affected: Clients that start watch streams with the `allowBookmarks=true` option and rely on the initial events list format.
127587.fix: The Bookmark event now includes a new annotation `kubernetes.io/initial-events-list-blueprint` that carries an empty, version‑ed list encoded in the request's preferred format (protobuf, JSON, CBOR) and base64‑encoded. This provides clients with the blueprint of the initial events list.
127587.impact: Clients can reliably discover the expected format of the initial events list from a Bookmark, improving compatibility and reducing errors when establishing watch streams, especially for features built on KEP‑3157.

127673.problem: The CustomResourceFieldSelectors feature was gated and required the `--feature-gates=CustomResourceFieldSelectors=true` flag on kube-apiserver binaries. Clusters that did not enable the flag could not use field selectors on custom resources.
127673.affected: Clusters running versions where CustomResourceFieldSelectors was still gated, especially those that did not set the feature‑gate flag, and any automation that added the flag to kube‑apiserver binaries.
127673.fix: The feature has been promoted to GA and is now enabled by default. The feature gate flag is no longer required and will be removed in a future release.
127673.impact: Administrators no longer need to modify kube-apiserver startup flags to use custom resource field selectors, simplifying cluster configuration and ensuring the feature works out‑of‑the‑box for all clusters.

127857.problem: The coordination.v1alpha1 API version was removed, but clusters may still contain coordination.v1alpha1 objects. During an upgrade, the API server rejects these unknown types, causing upgrade failures.
127857.affected: Clusters that have created coordination.v1alpha1 resources (such as Lease objects) and attempt to upgrade without first removing them.
127857.fix: The release replaces coordination.v1alpha1 with coordination.v1alpha2. Users must delete any existing coordination.v1alpha1 resources (e.g., Lease objects) before performing the upgrade so that only the new version is present.
127857.impact: Ensures a smooth upgrade path by preventing API incompatibility errors. Clusters that clean up the old objects upgrade without interruption; those that do not will encounter upgrade failures.

127981.problem: When the SELinuxMount feature (alpha) is enabled, Kubernetes will automatically mount pod volumes with a SELinux label. This can break workloads that rely on existing volume labels, and users have no way to prevent the relabeling during upgrades on SELinux-enabled clusters.
127981.affected: Clusters running with SELinux enabled that enable the SELinuxMount feature, and any pods that need to keep their original volume SELinux labels.
127981.fix: Introduces a new alpha field `seLinuxChangePolicy` in the Pod-level `securityContext` behind the SELinuxChangePolicy feature gate. When set, it allows a pod to opt out of the automatic SELinux label mounting, preserving the original volume labels.
127981.impact: Provides a safe upgrade path for clusters that enable SELinuxMount, preventing unexpected pod failures due to unwanted SELinux relabeling. Users on clusters without SELinux are unaffected.

128003.problem: Support for classic dynamic resource allocation (DRA) has been removed. Clusters that enabled the DRAControlPlaneController feature gate and have workloads (pods, deployments, etc.) using classic DRA, as well as existing PodSchedulingContext resources, will experience scheduling failures after upgrade because those resources cannot be deleted via the apiserver post‑upgrade.
128003.affected: Clusters with the DRAControlPlaneController feature gate enabled and workloads (pods, deployments, etc.) that rely on classic DRA, plus any existing PodSchedulingContext resources.
128003.fix: The feature gate and its controller have been dropped. Users must delete all workloads that depend on classic DRA and ensure all PodSchedulingContext resources are removed before performing the upgrade. After upgrade, only the structured parameters DRA model is available.
128003.impact: Any cluster that was using classic DRA must perform cleanup before upgrading, otherwise affected pods will remain unschedulable, leading to application downtime. The change simplifies DRA support to a single model, reducing future maintenance complexity.

128077.problem: NodeRestriction admission did not check that the audience requested by kubelet for a projected service account token matched the audience declared in the pod's volume spec, allowing potential misuse of service account tokens.
128077.affected: Clusters with the NodeRestriction admission plugin enabled and pods using projected service account token volumes (including kubelet image credential provider scenarios).
128077.fix: NodeRestriction now validates that the audience value requested by the kubelet is present in the pod spec's projected service account token volume. The validation is controlled by the ServiceAccountNodeAudienceRestriction feature gate, which is enabled by default.
128077.impact: Improves cluster security by ensuring kubelets can only obtain service account tokens for audiences that pods explicitly allow, preventing unauthorized token use. No functional changes for correctly configured workloads.

128101.problem: CEL expressions used in Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) were evaluated without any cost or runtime limits, allowing potentially expensive or malicious expressions to consume excessive CPU and delay scheduling or API responses.
128101.affected: Clusters that use DRA with CEL expressions for pod placement or custom resource allocation. Users who define complex or unbounded CEL rules are now protected from performance impact.
128101.fix: Implemented an upper bound on the evaluation cost and the number of runtime steps for CEL expressions. Both the kube-apiserver and kube-scheduler now enforce these limits during DRA evaluation.
128101.impact: Prevents runaway CEL evaluations that could degrade API server performance or scheduler latency, protecting clusters from accidental or deliberate denial‑of‑service conditions and ensuring more predictable scheduling behavior.

128170.problem: Pod preemption in the scheduler is performed synchronously, causing the scheduler to block while making API calls. This can increase scheduling latency, especially in clusters with many preemptible pods or high contention.
128170.affected: Clusters that use preemptible pods (e.g., low‑priority workloads) and experience scheduling delays due to synchronous preemption handling.
128170.fix: Introduces the `SchedulerAsyncPreemption` feature gate. When enabled, the scheduler triggers preemption API calls asynchronously, allowing the main scheduling loop to continue without waiting for those calls to complete.
128170.impact: Reduces scheduling latency and improves overall scheduler throughput for clusters that rely on preemptible pods. Users can opt‑in to the alpha feature to get better performance in busy environments.

128172.problem: Before this release the StructuredAuthorizationConfiguration feature gate was not GA, and the --authorization-config flag only supported the beta API version (apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1beta1). Users could not rely on a stable v1 schema for AuthorizationConfiguration.
128172.affected: Any cluster using kube-apiserver with the --authorization-config flag for custom authorization plugins; administrators configuring AuthorizationConfiguration files.
128172.fix: The feature gate is promoted to GA and the flag now accepts the v1 version of AuthorizationConfiguration (apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1) with identical semantics to v1beta1.
128172.impact: Clusters can now configure authorization using the stable v1 API without changes to the config file, benefiting from GA stability guarantees and simplifying future upgrades.

128240.problem: Drivers could not convey per‑device status information back to users because ResourceClaim.Status had no driver‑owned fields, limiting observability of allocated device health.
128240.affected: Workloads that use ResourceClaims for device allocation (e.g., DRA/CSI‑based pods) and the drivers managing those devices.
128240.fix: Introduced driver‑owned fields in ResourceClaim.Status that allow each allocated device to report its status data, enabling drivers (e.g., CSI) to publish health and other device‑specific metrics.
128240.impact: Users and cluster operators can now see device‑level status for allocated resources, improving troubleshooting, automated remediation, and overall reliability of workloads that depend on external devices.

128244.problem: Pods that use the new ReadWriteOncePod access mode do not honor the fsGroup and fsGroupChange settings, causing volumes to be mounted with root:root ownership and preventing container processes from writing to the volume.
128244.affected: Any pod or StatefulSet that uses a ReadWriteOncePod volume with a non‑zero fsGroup setting, including workloads using CSI drivers such as the AWS EBS CSI driver.
128244.fix: Implemented handling of fsGroup for ReadWriteOncePod volumes so that the volume is chowned according to the pod's securityContext before it is mounted.
128244.impact: Pods (especially StatefulSets) that rely on ReadWriteOncePod volumes can now correctly apply filesystem group ownership, eliminating write permission errors and ensuring expected security context behavior.

128247.problem: Prior to this change, the automatic deletion of PersistentVolumeClaims (PVCs) for StatefulSets was only available behind the beta feature gate `StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC`, requiring users to manually enable it and preventing its use in production environments.
128247.affected: Users running StatefulSets that need automatic PVC deletion, particularly those managing stateful workloads with dynamic storage. Both new and existing clusters benefit.
128247.fix: The feature gate `StatefulSetAutoDeletePVC` has been promoted from beta to stable (GA). It is now part of the stable API surface and enabled by default, allowing StatefulSets to automatically delete associated PVCs when the StatefulSet is deleted without additional configuration.
128247.impact: Clusters can safely rely on automatic PVC cleanup for StatefulSets in production, reducing manual storage management and preventing orphaned volumes. Existing workloads that enabled the beta gate continue to work unchanged, while new clusters get the behavior automatically.

128266.problem: In‑place vertical pod scaling was implemented using a generic PATCH on the Pod object, which lacked dedicated RBAC controls, was less clear, and could not be easily extended to other controller objects like Deployments or Jobs.
128266.affected: Users and controllers that perform in‑place pod vertical scaling, as well as developers of client libraries that need to request pod resource changes.
128266.fix: Introduced a new `/resize` subresource for Pods. Clients should now issue resize requests against `/api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/resize` instead of PATCH. The subresource includes its own RBAC verification and paves the way for similar resize endpoints on higher‑level workload objects.
128266.impact: Provides a clean, purpose‑built API for pod resource resizing, improves security via fine‑grained RBAC, and enables future support for resize operations on other workload resources. Existing clients need to update their code to call the new subresource.

128296.problem: kubectl's --subresource flag was limited to a predefined set of subresources, preventing users from accessing new subresources such as the `resize` subresource introduced for in‑place pod vertical scaling.
128296.affected: Users of kubectl who need to interact with custom subresources, especially those working with pod resource resizing and in‑place vertical scaling.
128296.fix: The CLI validation that restricted the values of the --subresource flag was removed, allowing any valid subresource name (e.g., `resize`) to be used with commands like `kubectl patch` and `kubectl edit`.
128296.impact: Operators and developers can now use kubectl to manually test and manage in‑place pod resource updates via the new resize subresource, improving usability and reducing the need for custom tooling.

128336.problem: Jobs created by CronJobs did not have a stable annotation indicating the exact time they were scheduled, making it hard for users to reliably track and correlate job execution times.
128336.affected: All workloads where CronJobs create Jobs; any tooling or scripts that need the schedule timestamp of a Job.
128336.fix: Introduces the stable annotation `batch.kubernetes.io/cronjob-scheduled-timestamp` on Job objects that are scheduled by CronJobs, replacing any previous beta or undocumented fields.
128336.impact: Users and operators can now programmatically read a consistent, versioned annotation to determine when a CronJob triggered a Job, improving observability, debugging, and integration with external tooling.

128374.problem: Cluster administrators could not control the maximum backoff delay for containers in CrashLoopBackOff, causing potentially long wait times before a container is retried after repeated crashes.
128374.affected: Any workload that experiences CrashLoopBackOff on a node, particularly those needing quicker restarts, and the node’s kubelet that manages the backoff timing.
128374.fix: Introduces a new feature gate `KubeletCrashLoopBackoffMax` and a kubelet config field `CrashLoopBackOff.MaxContainerRestartPeriod` (range 1s‑300s) that lets operators set the maximum backoff delay for restarts on a per‑node basis.
128374.impact: Operators can tune restart behavior to reduce downtime for crash‑looping workloads, improving reliability and allowing faster recovery on nodes where long backoff is undesirable.

128377.problem: The ContainerStatus.AllocatedResources field was exposed unconditionally, which could be read by components (e.g., scheduler) before the in‑place pod vertical scaling feature was fully ready, leading to incorrect scheduling decisions and potential resource over‑commitment. Additionally, kubelet handling of the field was inconsistent with the updated in‑place resize logic.
128377.affected: Users performing in‑place pod resource resizing (vertical scaling) and any scheduler or kubelet behavior that relies on the pod's allocated resources status.
128377.fix: The AllocatedResources status field is now hidden behind a new feature gate `InPlacePodVerticalScalingAllocatedStatus`. Kubelet now reads the field directly from the status manager, and other components only see it when the feature gate is enabled. References outside the kubelet have been shifted to use `status.resources` instead.
128377.impact: Clusters that enable in‑place pod vertical scaling will now get correct resource accounting and scheduling behavior, preventing oversubscription and eliminating a class of bugs where reduced resources could be incorrectly accepted. Users not enabling the feature see no change, preserving backward compatibility.

128396.problem: The ServiceAccount annotation "kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets" is deprecated. Users relying on this annotation to enforce that only mountable secrets are used may continue to see it but it will no longer have any effect in the future.
128396.affected: Clusters where ServiceAccount objects include the "kubernetes.io/enforce-mountable-secrets" annotation, and any workloads that depend on its enforcement behavior.
128396.fix: The annotation is now marked as deprecated (no removal deadline). Users should transition to isolating secret access by placing workloads in separate namespaces instead of using the annotation.
128396.impact: Prevents future reliance on a deprecated mechanism for secret isolation, encouraging a more robust namespace‑based isolation approach. Existing workloads continue to function, but new deployments should adopt the recommended practice to avoid surprises.

128407.problem: Pod specifications could only define resources at the container level, making it impossible to declare resources that apply to the entire pod (e.g., overhead or shared resources).
128407.affected: Any workload that needs pod‑level resource definitions, such as pods with shared side‑cars, overhead accounting, or custom controllers that set pod resources.
128407.fix: Introduced a new `resources` field under `spec` in the Pod API, allowing users to specify pod‑level resource requests and limits.
128407.impact: Enables accurate resource accounting and scheduling for pod‑wide resources, improves quota enforcement, and lets developers express overhead or shared resource needs directly in the pod manifest.

128601.problem: Opaque device configuration parameters for Device Resource Allocation (DRA) could be arbitrarily large, allowing requests that exceed reasonable size limits and potentially causing API server performance degradation or etcd storage issues.
128601.affected: Workloads and CSI drivers that use DRA with opaque device configuration parameters larger than 10 KiB. Cluster administrators deploying such drivers are directly impacted.
128601.fix: An admission controller now enforces a 10 KiB size limit on opaque device configuration parameters at admission time, rejecting overly large specifications.
128601.impact: Prevents excessively large DRA configuration payloads, protecting API server stability and etcd size while giving users a clear validation error when their device configs exceed the limit.

126720.problem: The DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion feature gate remained enabled by default after its deprecation announcement in v1.29, which does not give users a full year to transition.
126720.affected: Users who had the DisableNodeKubeProxyVersion gate enabled by default in clusters upgraded from v1.29 onward, and any workloads depending on that behavior.
126720.fix: Reverted the feature gate to its default-off state, ensuring it is disabled by default and giving users a full year before the field is cleared, as required by the Kubernetes deprecation policy.
126720.impact: Clusters that relied on the feature being enabled by default must now explicitly enable it if needed, preventing accidental usage after deprecation and aligning with policy timelines.

129544.problem: The previous limit allowed a maximum of 32 pods to share a single ResourceClaim, restricting workloads that needed more pods to use the same claim. Additionally, clusters that upgraded to the higher limit cannot be safely downgraded to version 1.32.0 because that version rejects more than 32 entries in the status.reservedFor field.
129544.affected: Clusters using Device Resource Allocation (DRA) where many pods need the same ResourceClaim, and any users planning to downgrade to Kubernetes 1.32.0 after enabling the higher limit.
129544.fix: The DRA API limit for pods per ResourceClaim has been increased to 256, allowing many more pods to share the same claim. The change also includes a compatibility note that downgrading to 1.32.0 is unsupported when the new limit is in use.
129544.impact: Workloads that require a large number of pods to share a single ResourceClaim can now scale up to 256 pods, improving flexibility for high‑density deployments. Administrators must be aware that clusters using this expanded limit cannot be downgraded to 1.32.0, preventing potential upgrade/downgrade issues.

129423.problem: No functional issue; this change updates the Go compiler version used to build Kubernetes binaries.
129423.affected: All Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kubelet, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) and developers who compile Kubernetes from source.
129423.fix: Kubernetes is now built with Go 1.23.4 instead of the prior Go version.
129423.impact: All Kubernetes components benefit from Go 1.23 security patches and performance improvements. Users and CI pipelines that build Kubernetes from source must have Go 1.23.4 installed.

129180.problem: Multipath-attached iSCSI and Fibre Channel devices that were partitioned failed to resolve correctly on nodes, causing storage provisioning or mounting errors.
129180.affected: Clusters using iSCSI or Fibre Channel storage with multipath configurations where the devices have partitions; primarily affects kubelet's volume management on the affected nodes.
129180.fix: The multipath handling logic was corrected so that partitioned iSCSI and Fibre Channel devices are now resolved properly during volume attachment.
129180.impact: Nodes can reliably use partitioned multipath iSCSI/FC disks, preventing pod startup failures and improving overall storage reliability for workloads that rely on these block devices.

129322.problem: kube-controller-manager panics when it processes a StatefulSet that has a negative revisionHistoryLimit value, causing the controller manager to crash.
129322.affected: Clusters with StatefulSet objects configured with a negative revisionHistoryLimit could experience a controller-manager panic, impacting the control plane and any StatefulSet workloads.
129322.fix: Added validation and safe handling for a negative revisionHistoryLimit in the StatefulSet controller, preventing the panic and ensuring the controller manager continues running.
129322.impact: Prevents controller-manager crashes that could disrupt StatefulSet management and affect overall cluster stability for clusters using an invalid (negative) revisionHistoryLimit.

129455.problem: The `kubeadm upgrade node` command ignored the `node.skipPhases` setting in `UpgradeConfiguration`, causing phases that users intended to skip to still be executed during node upgrades.
129455.affected: Clusters being upgraded with `kubeadm upgrade node` where the `node.skipPhases` option was used. Administrators performing node upgrades were affected.
129455.fix: The upgrade logic was updated so that `kubeadm upgrade node` now correctly respects the `node.skipPhases` configuration and skips the specified phases.
129455.impact: Users can now reliably control which upgrade phases run on a node, avoiding unnecessary actions, reducing upgrade time, and preventing unintended changes or downtime during node upgrades.

129429.problem: During a kubeadm upgrade, addons that were disabled in the ClusterConfiguration were still processed, causing upgrade failures or unnecessary operations.
129429.affected: Clusters managed with kubeadm where the ClusterConfiguration disables specific addons.
129429.fix: The kubeadm upgrade logic now checks the ClusterConfiguration and skips any addon marked as disabled, avoiding attempts to apply them.
129429.impact: Users upgrading clusters with kubeadm no longer encounter errors related to disabled addons, resulting in smoother and more reliable upgrade experiences.

129966.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go compiler, missing recent language/runtime fixes and security patches.
129966.affected: All users and CI pipelines that build or run Kubernetes binaries are affected, as the binaries are now produced with a newer Go toolchain.
129966.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.23.5, recompiling all Kubernetes components with the newer toolchain.
129966.impact: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, etc.) are now built with the latest Go version, bringing upstream bug fixes, security updates, and performance improvements to users without requiring code changes.

130078.problem: Kubernetes binaries were built with an older Go version; updating the build toolchain was needed to stay compatible with upstream Go releases and incorporate language and security improvements.
130078.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy) and any clusters running these binaries.
130078.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled using Go 1.23.6.
